header.description: NOT A SHIPPED CAUSALAB DOCUMENT. A hand-written CPU reduction of documents/das.json, produced for causalab-mini so the DAS path has something that can actually run on this machine. das.json itself is already minimal in protocol features (one layer, one k, no sweep), so nothing was removed from `method` except what a CPU-sized model forces. Exactly four changes against das.json, and nothing else: (1) model.key/revision -> the tiny random Llama that minimal_cpu.json pins (commit 9fb191250dd56d0ba7ec9785a025ed29c03d5998), because meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B does not fit CPU testing; (2) model.dtype bf16 -> fp32, because CPU bf16 matmuls are slow and the reference suites run these fixtures in fp32; (3) sites.target.layers [18] -> [0], because the tiny Llama has 2 layers; (4) the three dataset refs natural_domains_arithmetic/data/weekdays#train / #test -> weekdays/data#train / #test, the 4-row fixture table (2 train rows, 2 test rows) whose answers are single tokens under the tiny Llama's sentencepiece tokenizer. Every section, key, metric, featurizer and train field is das.json's, unchanged, including k=8 (note d=16 on this model, so the subspace is half the residual stream - a smoke test, not a result) and batch.pairs=16 (larger than the 2-row train split, so a batch is the whole split).
